questions.q: What's the main problem with a bare except: in a pipeline script?
options: It only catches exceptions that inherit from ValueError
It catches every exception, including ones like KeyboardInterrupt or a NameError from a typo that you actually want to see
Python does not allow a bare except clause to run at all
It automatically retries the failed operation forever
questions.explain: Catching specific exceptions means only anticipated failures are handled, while truly unexpected errors still surface.

questions.q: Why use exponential backoff (2 ** attempt seconds) between retries instead of a fixed delay?
options: It waits progressively longer after each failure instead of repeatedly hammering a struggling server at the same fixed interval
It is required syntax for the requests library
It makes the script run faster overall
It guarantees the call will never fail again
questions.explain: Giving a struggling service more time between attempts is more likely to succeed than retrying immediately and repeatedly.

questions.q: Why is silently continuing with an empty DataFrame after a failed file read a bad pattern?
options: It will always raise a different, unrelated exception later
The script 'works' without crashing but quietly loads zero rows, and nobody notices until a downstream report looks wrong
pandas does not allow an empty DataFrame to be created
This pattern is actually the recommended best practice for all pipelines
questions.explain: Failing loudly at the moment the problem happens is almost always better than quietly continuing with bad or missing data.

questions.q: What does re-raising an exception after logging it (inside an except block) accomplish for a scheduled script?
options: It converts the exception into a warning instead
The script exits with a non-zero status, letting a scheduler or monitoring tool detect that the run failed
It prevents the error from ever being logged
It automatically restarts the script immediately
questions.explain: A non-zero exit status is exactly what a scheduler or monitor checks for to flag a run as failed instead of assuming success.

questions.q: In the retry example, what happens if every attempt in max_attempts fails?
options: The function returns None with no error
The exception is re-raised after the final attempt, instead of being silently absorbed
The function retries indefinitely with no limit
The script automatically falls back to a cached result
questions.explain: After the last attempt fails, the loop re-raises so the caller knows the operation genuinely did not succeed.
